transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. It's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um... I guess I'm here because... well, I hope I'm in the right place for this, but mostly I just don't really feel like myself anymore. It's a little embarrassing to admit, honestly, and I really don't want you to think I'm just being lazy. But I've sort of stopped doing the things I usually do. I used to be pretty active—I'd go hiking, I was coaching, playing my guitar... but I just stopped all of it. I haven't even been calling people back lately. 

It sounds bad, I know, but some days I just sit in my small rental for hours. I know there are things I need to do, I'm completely aware of it, but I just... I can't seem to make myself start. I hope it's okay that I came in for that. Does that make sense?
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't really say that. I really hope I'm not giving the impression that I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself. I don't feel sad, or... or tearful, if that's what you mean by depressed. It's not a heavy, crying kind of feeling at all. 

I just... I kind of don't feel much of anything, honestly. It's more like a blankness. I know people get depressed and it's really awful for them, so I definitely don't want to claim that and make my situation sound worse than it is. I'm just sort of... neutral, I guess? Is it okay to describe it like that? I really hope I'm answering your question right.
Did this start after something stressful happened in your life?

Well, um... I suppose there was something. I really don't want to sound like I'm making excuses, because I know people go through hard things every day and handle it perfectly fine. But... I guess things kind of started unraveling for me a bit after my divorce. 

That's when I moved into the smaller rental I mentioned earlier. It was about... maybe a year and two months ago? I feel a little embarrassed even bringing it up, honestly, because I know a lot of guys go through that and just keep working and doing their normal routine. I definitely don't want you to think I'm just sitting around complaining about my personal life or using it as a crutch. Is... is that the kind of information you were looking for? I hope I'm not oversharing.
Are these problems still happening now, more than six months after the divorce?

Yes, um... yes, they are. I know it's been over a year—a year and two months, like I said—and I really should have bounced back by now. I hope you don't think I'm just wallowing or refusing to move on. I know guys who go through divorces and they're back on their feet in a month, so it's pretty embarrassing that I'm still... like this, after all this time. 

It really has been going on since I moved into that smaller place. I keep telling myself I need to snap out of it, and I really am trying, I promise. I just... I haven't quite gotten there yet. Is it... is it really bad that it's been going on this long? I hope I'm not a hopeless case or anything.
Before this started after your divorce, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt this same kind of loss of interest or emotional blankness for weeks at a time?

Oh, no... no, never anything like this before. I've always been a pretty steady guy, you know? I mean, with my job, you kind of have to be. You can't really afford to check out or go blank when people are relying on you to keep things safe. 

So, no, before the divorce, I was always... well, normal, I guess. I was engaged, interested in things, doing my job well. I really hope that shows that I'm usually a much more capable person than I seem right now. I've never been the type to just... stop caring or let things slide. Does that make sense? I just really want you to know that this isn't how I usually am.
Have you been feeling anxious or worried a lot lately?

Well, um... no, not really. I wouldn't say I've been anxious or worried. I hope that's okay? I know with everything going on, maybe it sounds strange that I'm not, but I've never really been a worrier. In my line of work, you kind of have to keep a level head and stay calm, so I try really hard not to let things get to me like that. 

I definitely don't sit around panicking or anything. I hope that's a good sign? I mean, I want to be as helpful as I can for your assessment, but I really haven't noticed feeling nervous or on edge. Is it normal that I'm not feeling anxious? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
